network.overall_strategy: This synthesis network follows literature-supported and plausible prebiotic chemistries for the formation of L-Proline from simple, prebiotically available compounds. The backbone is the experimentally supported cyanosulfidic photoredox route (Patel et al. 2015), with detection-based and inferred pathways from electric discharge, extraterrestrial residues, and mineral-catalyzed Strecker/ornithine/biochemical analogs included for completeness. All steps are constructed to conserve mass and charge, and mechanistic or environmental constraints and open problems are made explicit. Chirality amplification is represented in the final steps, as no abiotic route to enantioenriched L-proline is established.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-catalyzed coupling of HCN and acetylene to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Near-neutral to slightly basic pH; flow or staged addition

reactions.mechanism: Cu(I)-mediated nucleophilic addition of HCN to acetylene; elimination of proton to form acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Experimental step in Patel et al. 2015, Nature Chemistry; demonstrated but geochemically contested for Cu and acetylene supply ([1],[2],[4],[7],[8]).

reactions.name: Aza-Michael addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of ammonia across the activated alkene of acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Directly shown by Patel et al. 2015; no catalyst required ([1],[2],[4]).

reactions.name: Photoreduction (UV/H2S) of β-aminopropionitrile to 2-amino-3-hydroxypropanenitrile

conditions.other: UV irradiation; presence of H2S as photoreductant

reactions.mechanism: UV photolysis with H2S leads to reduction of the nitrile group to aldehyde, water serves as nucleophile, further HCN addition forms cyanohydrin.
reactions.reasoning: Directly outlined in Patel et al. 2015, mechanism and experimental ([1],[2],[4],[7]). Products and identities confirmed in mixture.

reactions.name: Thioamidation with H2S to produce α-hydroxythioamide
reactions.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of H2S to the nitrile/aldehyde group, forming thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Observed by Patel et al. 2015 ([1],[2],[4]); α-hydroxythioamide produced in mixture.

reactions.name: UV/H2S photodeoxygenation and cyclization to γ-butyrothiolactam

conditions.other: UV irradiation; reductant and ring closure

reactions.mechanism: Removal of oxo group by H2S-driven photoreduction, enabling intramolecular attack to close pyrrolidine ring as thioamide.
reactions.reasoning: Mechanistically explained and observed by Patel et al. 2015 ([1],[2],[4]).

reactions.name: Further UV/H2S reduction and strecker cyanation to yield pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile

conditions.other: UV irradiation, staged addition of HCN

reactions.mechanism: Photoreduction of thioamide to cyclic imine, then Strecker-type nucleophilic addition of HCN to form cyclic nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Partially direct and partially inferred mechanism per Patel et al., Figure 1 legend ([1],[2],[4],[5]). Atom balances preserve C/H/N/S.

reactions.name: Amination of pyrrolidine-2-carbonitrile to form proline aminonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Amination of the carbonitrile with ammonia to generate the α-amino group.
reactions.reasoning: Inferred as final productive step in Patel et al. 2015 ([1],[2],[4]); literature notes the aminonitrile is robust (Ritson 2021 [5]).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of proline aminonitrile to prolinamide

conditions.other: Mildly acidic or neutral aqueous conditions

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of nitrile group to amide; releases HCN; follows strecker chemistry principles.
reactions.reasoning: Step not reported in main Patel et al. paper but follows generic Strecker intermediacy ([1],[2],[4], speculative). Atom balance explicitly shown.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of prolinamide to L-proline
reactions.mechanism: Amide hydrolysis to carboxylic acid; releases ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Standard hydrolysis mechanism; step not demonstrated for proline but robust for other amino-acid amides ([1],[2],[4], speculative as no experimental report for this step).

reactions.name: Chiral amplification of L-proline (solid-liquid eutectic enrichment)
reactions.mechanism: Phase-driven separation of enantiomers; minor L-excess is enriched in solution below eutectic point; major D-enantiomer precipitates.
reactions.reasoning: Klussmann et al. 2006, Nature; applies only if any seed ee exists; best-case with prebiotic solvents is ~50% ee ([61],[62],[63]).

reactions.name: Alternative detection route: Strecker-type proline synthesis in spark discharge

conditions.other: Simulated prebiotic atmosphere; hydrolysis after synthesis

reactions.mechanism: Electric discharge generates reactive CN and NH intermediates, followed by hydrolysis; mechanistic intermediates not isolated.
reactions.reasoning: Proline detected among product mixture; mechanism inferred by analogy (Ring et al. 1972, Johnson et al. 2008, Parker et al. 2011 [12],[14],[16]).

reactions.name: Detection route: Proline released from extraterrestrial ice/hydrolyzed residue

conditions.other: Irradiated interstellar ice analogs; proline only after acid hydrolysis

reactions.mechanism: Radical combination in ices, generating complex organic polymers; proline released from macromolecules on hydrolysis.
reactions.reasoning: Detected only after hydrolysis (Muñoz Caro et al. 2002, Bernstein et al. 2002 [19],[20],[21]). Atom balance not determinable; route included as detection only.

reactions.name: Meteorite/asteroid (aqueous alteration) Strecker-like pathway to proline

conditions.other: Aqueous alteration of parent body materials

reactions.mechanism: Mineral or metal surface-mediated Strecker-like synthesis, followed by aqueous hydrolysis; no intermediates characterized for proline branch.
reactions.reasoning: Detection in Murchison, Bennu, meteorites; no mechanistic intermediates identified (Kvenvolden et al. 1970, Glavin et al. 2025 [24]). Atom balance not demonstrable.

reactions.name: Metabolism-inspired: Reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate to L-glutamate

conditions.other: Alkaline vent, pH ~9–11; H2 supply required

reactions.mechanism: Nonenzymatic reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate by ammonium ion in presence of H2 and metals/minerals.
reactions.reasoning: Step demonstrated in Kitadai et al. 2019, Kaur et al. 2024 [29],[31]; only glutamate formation established.

reactions.name: Speculative: Glutamate reduction to glutamate-5-semialdehyde
reactions.mechanism: Partial reduction of glutamate carboxyl group to aldehyde; amine group preserved.
reactions.reasoning: No prebiotic demonstration for this step (see discussion in research findings); included as a speculative, metabolism-inspired conversion ([10],[32],[34]).

reactions.name: Spontaneous cyclization: Glutamate-5-semialdehyde to P5C
reactions.mechanism: Spontaneous nucleophilic attack of the α-amino group on the aldehyde carbon yields cyclic imine (pyrroline-5-carboxylate).
reactions.reasoning: Well-established in biology; nonenzymatic cyclization occurs robustly (Smith & Greenberg 1956 [35]).

reactions.name: Speculative: Reduction of P5C to L-proline
reactions.mechanism: Reduction of imine to secondary amine; forms proline.
reactions.reasoning: No demonstrated prebiotic reduction of P5C to proline exists (reviewed extensively in research findings). Placeholder for future discovery ([11],[32],[35]).

reactions.name: Ornithine cyclodeamination to L-proline (speculative/hydrothermal)
reactions.mechanism: Cyclization and elimination of ammonia from ornithine side-chain; forms L-proline.
reactions.reasoning: Observed as minor degradation product in Vallentyne 1968 (open to question); modern data lacking ([44],[45]).

reactions.name: Arginine degradation to proline (speculative/hydrothermal)
reactions.mechanism: Loss of guanidine group and side-chain cyclization to ornithine, then to proline.
reactions.reasoning: Degradation noted in Vallentyne 1968 and Körner et al. 2021 ([44],[45]); product identity not universally confirmed.

reactions.name: Formation of ornithine from glutamate (speculative, prebiotic side-chain extension)
reactions.mechanism: Pipe-side chain amidination and reduction, removing one CO2 equivalent, yields ornithine.
reactions.reasoning: Not demonstrated; aligned with speculative glutamate→ornithine metabolism ([10],[34]).

reactions.name: Guanidinylation of β-aminopropionitrile to arginine aminonitrile (competing sink)

conditions.other: Cyanamide present; diverts pathway from proline

reactions.mechanism: Addition of cyanamide to amino group forms arginine aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Described by Patel et al. as competing with proline route when cyanamide is present ([1],[2],[4]).

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic photoredox route to proline (Patel backbone)
pathways.description: Mass- and atom-conserving, stepwise literature-supported route from HCN and acetylene to L-proline, via acrylonitrile, aminonitrile intermediates, and photoreduction.

pathways.name: Cyanamide (arginine) competing branch
pathways.description: Cyanamide present at acrylonitrile stage intercepts β-aminopropionitrile to form arginine aminonitrile, diverting from proline.

pathways.name: Metabolism-inspired Glu/P5C route (speculative)
pathways.description: Reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate to glutamate; reduction to GSA, cyclization to P5C; speculative reduction to proline.

pathways.name: Ornithine/arginine cyclodeamination to proline (speculative, hydrothermal)
pathways.description: Ornithine or arginine undergo hydrothermal cyclodeamination/pyrolysis to proline.

pathways.name: Surface electric discharge Strecker route
pathways.description: Electric discharge on simple gases produces HCN, aldehydes, and ammonia, leading to Strecker chemistry and formation of proline (inferred mechanism).

pathways.name: Extraterrestrial interstellar ice photolysis and hydrolysis detection route
pathways.description: Photolysis and hydrolysis of simulated planetary/icy interstellar ices generate (hydrolyzed) proline.

pathways.name: Meteorite/asteroid aqueous alteration detection route
pathways.description: Aqueous alteration of planetary materials (meteorites, asteroids) provides surface for proline generation, detected in residue.

pathways.name: Speculative formation of ornithine from glutamate, then cyclodeamination
pathways.description: Glutamate is transformed to ornithine (speculative), then cyclodeaminated to proline under hydrothermal conditions.

pathways.name: Arginine degradation to proline via ornithine (hydrothermal, speculative)
pathways.description: Arginine undergoes guanidine group loss and subsequent cyclization through ornithine to yield proline.

pathways.name: Proline synthesis via Strecker route and hydrolysis (meteorite-origin simulation)
pathways.description: Generic Strecker chemistry post-delivery on meteorites simulating planetary aqueous environment, yielding proline after hydrolysis.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P1 (Cyanosulfidic photoredox, Patel backbone) is the most literature-supported mechanistic route, and the steps correspond to those described by Patel et al. (2015). Environmental assignment and catalytic agents largely fit the reported surface chemistry scenario. However, the reaction balance check reveals that most key steps (rxn_002, rxn_003, rxn_004, rxn_005, rxn_006, rxn_008, rxn_009) are unbalanced as written, indicating problems with mass/charge accounting or missing/byproduct species. This is a major chemical feasibility concern, as atom conservation is essential. The final hydrolysis and chiral amplification steps are conceptually valid but lack demonstrated yields (Patel only reports to the aminonitrile). To improve, all unbalanced reactions should be explicitly balanced with all byproducts named. Overall, the route is sound in design but not fully defensible chemically until the balance errors are fixed.
suggestions: Explicitly balance all intermediate steps with correct byproducts (e.g., S, NH3, CO2, H2)
Consult the original Patel et al. SI or correct inferred steps using elementary reactions
Clearly identify all byproduct species wherever possible

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P2 follows the competing arginine branch of the cyanosulfidic framework, where cyanamide diverts intermediates toward arginine aminonitrile. Reaction balance issues (rxn_002, rxn_021 both unbalanced and missing atoms, notably C, O, or N), and the lack of clear demonstration that this actually yields proline (vs. sinks flux into arginine) weaken the pathway. Literature also flags the guanidinylation as a documented alternate thread but does not show this as a productive proline route. The pathway is not robust as written.
suggestions: Clarify whether any steps actually yield proline, or only siphon intermediates away
Balance reactions fully and isolate all products/byproducts

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P3 is a metabolism-inspired branch (Glu → GSA → P5C → Pro) that is speculative, with demonstrated chemistry only for the reductive amination of α-ketoglutarate to Glu. GSA formation from Glu and P5C reduction to Pro are not known outside enzymatic or harsh chemical systems and are not supported by prebiotic chemistry literature, which is correctly acknowledged. Several steps are flagged as unbalanced. The pathway is appropriate to include for completeness, but not as a robust prebiotic solution.
suggestions: Mark speculative steps explicitly in diagrams
Highlight open experimental gaps and suggest target experiments for missing steps

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P4 (ornithine/arginine cyclodeamination to proline) is included as a speculative, hydrothermal route. Literature review confirms only one dated experimental hint for nonenzymatic ornithine/arginine to proline conversion, and even this is unconfirmed and possibly ambiguous. Reaction balances are off in key steps (rxn_019). Inclusion is justified for completeness, but these cannot raise overall network confidence.
suggestions: Indicate the uncertainty in node annotations
Update based on any future demonstrations of relevant steps

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P5 (electric discharge Strecker-type route) is literature-aligned as a detection pathway for proline in Miller-type experiments, but with no resolved mechanism or intermediate isolation for proline. The core reaction (rxn_011) is highly unbalanced with major atom-count errors. As these routes are 'detection routes' rather than mechanisms, this is acceptable for inclusion but limits pathway confidence.
suggestions: Specify that this is a detection, not mechanistic, route
Disclose the atom/charge balancing limitations due to unknown mechanism

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P6 reflects extraterrestrial/ice photolysis and hydrolysis experiments, from which proline is detected but the mechanism is unknown. rxn_012 is unbalanced, but since this step represents an analytic detection, that is reasonable. The pathway is properly annotated as a detection route; confidence cannot be higher than moderate.
suggestions: Ensure all such routes are labeled as detections

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P7 covers meteorite/asteroid alteration, a detection-based route. rxn_013 is far from balanced but is defensible for detection-style pathways. As with P6, confidence is limited but proper inclusion is justified for comparison.
suggestions: Label route as detection only, not mechanistic

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P8 (ornithine from glutamate, then cyclodeamination) is speculative and incompletely chemically supported. No prebiotic demonstration exists for side-chain extension with cyanamide, nor for the cyclization. Problematic (unbalanced) reaction nodes (rxn_020, rxn_019). Proper as a speculative branch but not as a main route.
suggestions: Highlight speculative nature in diagrams and text
Balance all reactions for future versions

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P9 (arginine degradation to proline via ornithine) is speculative and based on literature observations from hydrothermal pyrolysis of arginine. Reaction balance issues persist, and mechanistic steps are not demonstrated for Pro. Inclusion is defensible for context but cannot be the best route.

P10 is a detection-based Strecker/hydrolysis route, similar to P5 but relevant to simulated meteorite aqueous alteration. As before, lack of intermediate or balanced step detail limits chemical feasibility, but its inclusion for completeness is appropriate.
suggestions: Declare detection-mode routes and avoid implying mechanism

evaluation.network_feedback: The synthesis network for L-proline is well-documented, includes all major literature-supported and detection-verified routes, and is exemplary in coverage. However, severe chemical feasibility shortfalls, mainly unbalanced reactions in the main cyanosulfidic path (and all alternative/mechanistic branches), lower overall confidence. The backbone (P1) is structurally and environmentally appropriate and the only stepwise literature-backed mechanism, but mass/charge conservation failures across most key steps preclude full approval. Detection- or metabolism-inspired branches are appropriately flagged as non-mechanistic or speculative but do not compensate for the mass balance errors. To raise the network to approval, all mechanistically modeled reactions must be explicitly balanced with complete atom accounting, or missing species must be named. Annotating speculative steps and detection-only routes as such is good practice and should be maintained.
